prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 家常红烧肉配料表 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 4 columns × 9 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "食材" · longest unbreakable word 14px · one-line width 40px
  col 2: header "用量（克）" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 67px
  col 3: header "处理方式" · longest unbreakable word 27px · one-line width 208px
  col 4: header "备注" · longest unbreakable word 27px · one-line width 160px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 480px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 479px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 480px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A kitchen reference card: eight ingredients for 家常红烧肉, each with a quantity and a short prep instruction plus an advisory note. It is consulted mid-cooking, not read as prose, so lookup speed and unambiguous quantities matter more than compactness.","reading":"Vertical scan down col 1 to locate an ingredient, then a short rightward hop to its amount, then the prep instruction, then optionally the note. Comparison happens down the amount column (500 vs 15 vs 5) and across the two prose columns, which are read only one row at a time. Rows are the unit, so every row should keep its four cells visually on the same band and prose should wrap rather than push a row apart.","groups":["col 1 + col 2: ingredient and its quantity are one measure unit ('what' + 'how much') and must be read together, so they should stay narrow and adjacent with no wrapping between them","col 3 + col 4: both are free prose; 处理方式 is the operative instruction, 备注 is secondary/advisory, so they may be traded against each other but not against cols 1–2"],"keep_intact":["ingredient names in col 1 (五花肉, 大葱, 冰糖 …) — never break a 2–3 character name","all amounts in col 2: 500, 15, 20, 25, 30, 5 and the words 适量 / 少许 must sit on one line","the header 用量（克） should stay unbroken so the unit is not orphaned from the number it qualifies","numeral+unit tokens inside prose such as 3厘米 and 两次 should not be split mid-token"],"may_wrap":["处理方式 sentences (切3厘米见方块，冷水下锅焯净血沫 / 焯水和炖煮时分两次加入) — 2 lines is acceptable","备注 sentences (选肥瘦三层分明的五花肉 / 老姜去腥效果更好) — advisory, can absorb 2–3 lines without hurting the lookup","the header 处理方式 / 备注 may wrap only as a last resort; both fit at 27px unbreakable"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[61,88,179,151],"idea":"Lock cols 1–2 at their exact one-line minimum so no ingredient or amount can ever wrap, then split the remaining 330px between the two prose columns in proportion to their natural one-line widths (208:160), giving both roughly two lines per row."},{"name":"B","widths":[61,88,216,114],"idea":"Action-forward: spend almost all slack on 处理方式 so most prep instructions finish on a single line and the cook can act immediately, letting the purely advisory 备注 wrap to two or three lines."},{"name":"C","widths":[80,98,172,129],"idea":"Scan-axis comfort: give the ingredient and amount columns extra breathing room (wider gutters around the numbers) to speed vertical lookup and comparison, accepting that both prose columns wrap a little more."}]}
